title: Lossless Vocabulary Reduction for Auto-Regressive Language Models
claim: A model over a large vocabulary can be inductively converted into an equivalent one over a smaller sub-vocabulary without losing accuracy.
layout: Left LM-before/after stack, middle distributions, right dashed formula and nested-tokenization boxes
description: On the left, two stacked language-model panels are joined by a down arrow labeled 'Lossless Vocabulary Reduction'. The top one is a grey head icon, a language model over V. It reads the text "'万' is the unit of 10,000 in" and has next-token candidates Japan 0.2, Japanese 0.1 and China 0.2. The bottom one is a blue head icon, a language model over V_sub. It reads the same text split into finer tokens and has candidates Ja 0.3, Ch 0.3 and En 0.01. A blue arrow leads from the bottom distribution to a blue dashed box on the upper right. That box holds the formulas for p_{V→V_sub}(y_{k+1}|y_{1:k}) as a normalized ratio of sums. A red dashed box below it shows nested tokenization. It maps candidate words like Japan and Japanese onto sub-vocabulary token sequences. Blue and red color-code the formulas and the matching boxes.
caption: Overview of lossless vocabulary reduction. Instead of sampling tokens from the original next-token distribution over $\mathcalV$, we can inductively compute and sample from the equivalent distribution over the sub-vocabulary $\mathcalVsub$ while keeping its accuracy. See [ref] for notations and details.
abstract: Tokenization -- the process of decomposing a given text into a sequence of subwords called tokens -- is one of the key components in the development of language models. Particularly, auto-regressive language models generate texts token by token, i.e., by predicting the next-token distribution given the previous ones, and thus tokenization directly affects their efficiency in text generation. Since each language model has their own vocabulary as a set of possible tokens, they struggle to cooperate with each other at the level of next-token distributions such as model ensemble. In this paper, we establish a theoretical framework of lossless vocabulary reduction, which efficiently converts a given auto-regressive language model into the one with an arbitrarily small vocabulary without any loss in accuracy. This framework allows language models with different tokenization to cooperate with each other efficiently by reduction to their maximal common vocabulary. Specifically, we empirically demonstrate its applicability to model ensemble with different tokenization.
